name: Reduce Checkout Kit web production JavaScript

description: Baseline build could not start because platforms/web dependencies are not provisioned (vite not found).
Fresh origin/main baseline after provisioning dependencies; standard web production build emitted one runtime file and passed declaration/manifest generation.

Derive telemetry's protocol-method Set from the existing generated notification/request catalogs instead of emitting 15 duplicate wire-method strings. 42,204 -> 41,895 bytes; standard build and 75 TypeScript protocol tests passed.

Expose individually tree-shakeable protocol descriptors and consume them directly in web. Build emitted 41,674 bytes but declaration generation reported stale protocol .d.ts exports, so the experiment is invalid until declarations are regenerated.

Mark individually exported generated descriptors pure so Rollup can prune unused protocol request codecs. The result regressed the retained 41,895-byte bundle to 41,914 bytes, so discard the descriptor-export approach.

Store only protocol wire names in the generated rename table and derive their camelCase TypeScript names during codec traversal, with codegen validation that every generated name is derivable. 41,895 -> 39,058 bytes; standard build and all 75 TypeScript protocol tests passed.

Index generated protocol model references numerically, reducing the build to 37,029 bytes, but six internal codec tests still called the changed private runtime helper with model-name strings. Update those tests to use generated model IDs before evaluating.

Replace generated protocol model-name references and object keys with deterministic numeric model IDs while preserving labels for validation errors. 39,058 -> 37,029 bytes; standard build and all 75 TypeScript protocol tests passed.
Explicitly use Vite's esbuild minifier to test whether it removes Rolldown region formatting. It produced 71,154 bytes versus 37,029, so keep the existing Oxc/default minifier.

Enable Oxc code generation in Rolldown's library output minifier. Vite 8 intentionally defaulted ES-library minification to compress/mangle without codegen, leaving formatting and region comments. 37,029 -> 29,397 bytes; standard build and all 302 web tests passed.

Expose generated protocol descriptors individually with valid pure annotations and have web consume only its nine handlers. It saved just 140 bytes (29,397 -> 29,257) while significantly expanding generated/public wiring, so discard as poor complexity-to-size tradeoff.

Dictionary-encode repeated protocol wire field names and numeric-tag generated rename traversal nodes. 29,397 -> 28,402 bytes; gzip moved from 9,750 to 9,844 bytes, while standard build and all 75 TypeScript protocol tests passed.

Encode the generated protocol rename spine as a compact printable string and reconstruct it once in the codec runtime, with generator bounds validation and a late-model regression test. 28,402 -> 27,610 bytes; gzip moved from 9,844 to 9,889 bytes, standard build passed, and all 76 TypeScript protocol tests passed.
Join the generated wire-field dictionary into one delimiter-separated string and split at startup. Oxc produced identical 27,610-byte JavaScript and gzip worsened by 10 bytes, so discard.

Decode compact rename-map symbols arithmetically from ASCII code points instead of shipping the 92-character encoding alphabet. 27,610 -> 27,545 bytes and gzip 9,889 -> 9,825 bytes; standard build and all 76 TypeScript protocol tests passed.

Unify telemetry export success and exception handling so measurement restoration, backoff updates, and active-request cleanup share one path; strengthen the failure test to verify restored measurements retry during shutdown. 27,545 -> 27,498 bytes and gzip 9,825 -> 9,811 bytes; standard build and all 13 telemetry tests passed.

Make telemetry flush async so immediate stopped, empty, and backoff branches return booleans directly instead of constructing explicit resolved promises. 27,498 -> 27,450 bytes and gzip 9,811 -> 9,795 bytes; standard build and all 13 telemetry tests passed.

Apply shared telemetry product/platform attributes inside the counter recorder instead of wrapping all three counter call sites. 27,450 -> 27,432 bytes and gzip 9,795 -> 9,794 bytes; standard build and all 13 telemetry tests passed.

Inline shared product/platform attributes into the histogram and counter recording paths to remove the attribute helper. JavaScript regressed by 1 byte (27,432 -> 27,433), despite gzip improving by 9 bytes, so discard on the primary metric.

Represent protocol codec traversal direction as a boolean instead of repeated decode/encode string values. 27,432 -> 27,387 bytes and gzip 9,794 -> 9,786 bytes; standard build and all 76 TypeScript protocol tests passed.

Replace per-object rename lookup Maps with nested scans over rename entries. It saved only 30 bytes (27,387 -> 27,357) and 18 gzip bytes while changing traversal from indexed lookup to O(fields × entries), so discard the performance risk for a marginal gain.

Call the shared navigation-duration recorder directly at its two success/failure sites instead of retaining one-use private wrappers. 27,387 -> 27,357 bytes and gzip 9,786 -> 9,770 bytes; standard build and 112 focused web protocol/window tests passed. Also refresh the autoresearch experiment summary.

Rebase the retained optimizations onto current main while preserving newly added ProtocolValidationError exports, own-property required-field checks, nested string validation, and undefined normalization. Current-main validation increased the retained bundle from 27,357 to 27,839 bytes, still below the 27.6 KiB stretch target; standard build and all 89 TypeScript protocol tests passed.

Size-only comparison for operator-required review fixes: cache reusable rename lookups, support escaped base-91 integers through MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, and extract a pure decoder with synthetic compatibility tests. 27,839 -> 27,953 JS bytes; 9,963 -> 9,998 gzip bytes; standard build and 117 protocol tests passed. Not a size improvement, hence discard classification; DO NOT revert the code: these are explicitly approved correctness/performance fixes, retained independently of the optimization loop.
